question: What are the patient's diagnosis for those who has lower red blood blood cell? State their ID and age.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1."Diagnosis", t1."ID", EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1."Birthday" AS TIMESTAMP)) AS Age FROM bird_thrombosis_prediction.Patient AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_thrombosis_prediction.Laboratory AS t2 ON t1."ID" = t2."ID" WHERE t2."RBC" < 3.5
raw_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  t1."ID",
  t1."Diagnosis",
  DATE_PART('year', AGE(CURRENT_DATE, TO_DATE(t1."Birthday", 'YYYY-MM-DD'))) AS age
FROM bird_thrombosis_prediction.Patient AS t1
INNER JOIN bird_thrombosis_prediction.Laboratory AS t2
  ON t1."ID" = t2."ID"
WHERE t2."RBC" < 3.5;
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.Diagnosis, T1.ID, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM T1.Birthday) AS Age FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RBC < 3.5
gold_execution_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1."Diagnosis", T1."ID", EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CURRENT_TIMESTAMP) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(T1."Birthday" AS TIMESTAMP)) AS Age FROM "Patient" AS T1 INNER JOIN "Laboratory" AS T2 ON T1."ID" = T2."ID" WHERE T2."RBC" < 3.5

A patient count requires distinct patient identity, not a count of multiplied lab/examination pairs. Registered stored-row key: ID, Date.

```sql
JOIN "bird_thrombosis_prediction"."Laboratory" AS "Laboratory"
```

question: In Scotland Premier League, which away team won the most during the 2010 season?
sql: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM bird_european_football_2."Match" AS m JOIN bird_european_football_2."League" AS l ON m.league_id = l.id JOIN bird_european_football_2."Team" AS t ON m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id WHERE l.name = 'Scotland Premier League' AND m.season = '2009/2010' AND m.away_team_goal > m.home_team_goal GROUP BY t.team_long_name ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: What are the speed in which attacks are put together of the top 4 teams with the highest build Up Play Speed?
sql: SELECT "buildUpPlaySpeed" FROM bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes ORDER BY "buildUpPlaySpeed" DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 4

question: Give the name of the league with the highest matches of all time and how many matches were played in the said league.
sql: SELECT t1.name, COUNT(t2.id) FROM bird_european_football_2.League AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name ORDER BY COUNT(t2.id) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql: SELECT t1.name, COUNT(t2.id) FROM bird_european_football_2.League AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name ORDER BY COUNT(t2.id) DESC LIMIT 1;
gold_sql: SELECT t2.name, t1.max_count FROM League AS t2 JOIN (SELECT league_id, MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT league_id, COUNT(id) AS cnt FROM Match GROUP BY league_id) AS subquery GROUP BY league_id ORDER BY MAX(cnt) DESC LIMIT 1) AS t1 ON t1.league_id = t2.id
gold_execution_sql: SELECT t2."name", t1.max_count FROM "League" AS t2 JOIN (SELECT "league_id", MAX(cnt) AS max_count FROM (SELECT "league_id", COUNT("id") AS cnt FROM "Match" GROUP BY "league_id") AS subquery GROUP BY "league_id" ORDER BY MAX(cnt) DESC LIMIT 1) AS t1 ON t1."league_id" = t2."id"

question: List the long name of teams with above-average build-up play passing in 2012.
sql: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM bird_european_football_2.Team AS t JOIN bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes AS ta ON t.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id WHERE ta.date LIKE '2012%' AND ta."buildUpPlayPassing" > (SELECT AVG(Team_Attributes."buildUpPlayPassing") FROM bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes WHERE date LIKE '2012%')
raw_sql: SELECT t.team_long_name FROM bird_european_football_2.Team AS t JOIN bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes AS ta ON t.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id WHERE ta.date LIKE '2012%' AND ta."buildUpPlayPassing" > (SELECT AVG("buildUpPlayPassing") FROM bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes WHERE date LIKE '2012%')
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT t4.team_long_name FROM Team_Attributes AS t3 INNER JOIN Team AS t4 ON t3.team_api_id = t4.team_api_id WHERE SUBSTR(t3."date", 1, 4) = '2012' AND t3.buildUpPlayPassing > (SELECT CAST(SUM(t2.buildUpPlayPassing) AS REAL) / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) FROM Team AS t1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.team_api_id = t2.team_api_id WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(t2."date" AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2012')
gold_execution_sql: SELECT DISTINCT t4."team_long_name" FROM "Team_Attributes" AS t3 INNER JOIN "Team" AS t4 ON t3."team_api_id" = t4."team_api_id" WHERE SUBSTRING(t3."date" FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' AND t3."buildUpPlayPassing" > (SELECT CAST(SUM(t2."buildUpPlayPassing") AS REAL) / NULLIF(COUNT(t1."id"), 0) FROM "Team" AS t1 INNER JOIN "Team_Attributes" AS t2 ON t1."team_api_id" = t2."team_api_id" WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(t2."date" AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2012')

table_hits.description:
BIRD european_football_2 table Team_Attributes; foreign keys: team_api_id -> Team.team_api_id
[Public business definition]
Dated team playing-style observations linked by team_api_id/team_fifa_api_id. A team can have multiple observations. Numeric buildUpPlaySpeed and its categorical buildUpPlaySpeedClass differ; buildup, chance creation and defense attributes have separate meanings. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Team
[Public business definition]
Team identity records with API identifiers and long/short names. Team names are identity attributes; team style ratings are dated observations in Team_Attributes. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Country
[Public business definition]
Country lookup entities referenced by leagues and matches. Country name describes the country; league name and team name identify different business entities. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Match; foreign keys: country_id -> Country.id, league_id -> League.id, home_team_api_id -> Team.team_api_id, away_team_api_id -> Team.team_api_id
[Public business definition]
Individual football matches with season, stage, date, league/country and separate home/away team roles. home_team_api_id and away_team_api_id identify those roles; home_team_goal and away_team_goal are the respective scores. season is a stored season label, while date identifies a calendar date. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Player
[Public business definition]
Player identity and physical profile records. player_api_id links to ratings and lineup references; player_name need not uniquely identify a player. Birthday, height and weight are profile attributes, separate from dated skill ratings. Registered stored-row key: id.

question: List the top 10 players' names whose heights are above 180 in descending order of average heading accuracy.
sql: SELECT t1.player_name FROM bird_european_football_2.Player AS t1 JOIN bird_european_football_2.Player_Attributes AS t2 ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id WHERE t1.height > 180 GROUP BY t1.player_api_id, t1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(t2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT
  t1.player_name
FROM bird_european_football_2.Player AS t1
JOIN bird_european_football_2.Player_Attributes AS t2
  ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id
WHERE
  t1.height > 180
GROUP BY
  t1.player_api_id,
  t1.player_name
ORDER BY
  AVG(t2.heading_accuracy) DESC
```

question: List the name of leagues in which the average goals by the home team is higher than the away team in the 2009/2010 season.
sql: SELECT t1.name FROM bird_european_football_2.League AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2009/2010' GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name HAVING AVG(t2.home_team_goal) > AVG(t2.away_team_goal)

question: Who has the highest average finishing rate between the highest and shortest football player?
sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM bird_european_football_2."Player" AS T1 JOIN bird_european_football_2."Player_Attributes" AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = (SELECT MAX(height) FROM bird_european_football_2."Player") OR T1.height = (SELECT MIN(height) FROM bird_european_football_2."Player") GROUP BY T1.player_name, T1.player_api_id ORDER BY AVG(T2.finishing) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM bird_european_football_2."Player" AS T1 JOIN bird_european_football_2."Player_Attributes" AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = (SELECT MAX(height) FROM bird_european_football_2."Player") OR T1.height = (SELECT MIN(height) FROM bird_european_football_2."Player") GROUP BY T1.player_name, T1.player_api_id ORDER BY AVG(T2.finishing) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1;
gold_sql: SELECT A FROM (SELECT AVG(finishing) AS result, 'Max' AS A FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = (SELECT MAX(height) FROM Player) UNION SELECT AVG(finishing) AS result, 'Min' AS A FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height = (SELECT MIN(height) FROM Player)) AS subquery ORDER BY result DESC LIMIT 1
gold_execution_sql: SELECT A FROM (SELECT AVG("finishing") AS result, 'Max' AS A FROM "Player" AS T1 INNER JOIN "Player_Attributes" AS T2 ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id" WHERE T1."height" = (SELECT MAX("height") FROM "Player") UNION SELECT AVG("finishing") AS result, 'Min' AS A FROM "Player" AS T1 INNER JOIN "Player_Attributes" AS T2 ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id" WHERE T1."height" = (SELECT MIN("height") FROM "Player")) AS subquery ORDER BY result DESC LIMIT 1

question: Give the name of the league had the most matches in the 2008/2009 season?
sql: SELECT t1.name FROM bird_european_football_2.League AS t1 JOIN bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2008/2009' GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(match_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 WHERE t2.season = '2008/2009' GROUP BY t2.league_id) AS subquery)
raw_sql: SELECT t1.name FROM bird_european_football_2.League AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_european_football_2.Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2008/2009' GROUP BY t1.id, t1.name ORDER BY count(*) DESC LIMIT 1;
gold_sql: SELECT t1.name FROM League AS t1 JOIN Match AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.league_id WHERE t2.season = '2008/2009' GROUP BY t1.name HAVING COUNT(t2.id) = (SELECT MAX(match_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(t2.id) AS match_count FROM Match AS t2 WHERE t2.season = '2008/2009' GROUP BY t2.league_id) AS subquery)

```sql
SELECT
  ta."chanceCreationPassing",

FROM bird_european_football_2.Team_Attributes AS ta
```

question: State the name of the most strongest player.
sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM bird_european_football_2.Player AS T1 JOIN bird_european_football_2.Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T2.strength IS NOT NULL ORDER BY T2.strength DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT
  T1.player_name
FROM bird_european_football_2.Player AS T1
JOIN bird_european_football_2.Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id
WHERE
  T2.strength IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY

LIMIT 1;
```

table_hits.description:
BIRD european_football_2 table Player_Attributes; foreign keys: player_api_id -> Player.player_api_id
[Public business definition]
Dated player rating observations identified by a rating record id and linked through player_api_id/player_fifa_api_id. Multiple dates may exist for one player. overall_rating, potential, strength, finishing and other attributes measure distinct qualities; an observation count is not a distinct player count. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Player
[Public business definition]
Player identity and physical profile records. player_api_id links to ratings and lineup references; player_name need not uniquely identify a player. Birthday, height and weight are profile attributes, separate from dated skill ratings. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Match; foreign keys: country_id -> Country.id, league_id -> League.id, home_team_api_id -> Team.team_api_id, away_team_api_id -> Team.team_api_id
[Public business definition]
Individual football matches with season, stage, date, league/country and separate home/away team roles. home_team_api_id and away_team_api_id identify those roles; home_team_goal and away_team_goal are the respective scores. season is a stored season label, while date identifies a calendar date. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Country
[Public business definition]
Country lookup entities referenced by leagues and matches. Country name describes the country; league name and team name identify different business entities. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table Team
[Public business definition]
Team identity records with API identifiers and long/short names. Team names are identity attributes; team style ratings are dated observations in Team_Attributes. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD european_football_2 table League; foreign keys: country_id -> Country.id
[Public business definition]
League entities associated with country_id. Matches reference a league through league_id. League records are not match observations or seasons. Registered stored-row key: id.

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table qualifying; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver qualifying results at a race, including qualifying position and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 segment times. Later segment times can be absent when the driver did not advance. These are qualifying times and positions, not the race finishing result.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorResults; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor results for individual races, relating a race and constructor. points are awarded for the race result, whereas constructorStandings points are cumulative championship snapshots. status belongs to the constructor race result, not the driver status lookup. Registered stored-row key: constructorResultsId.

BIRD formula_1 table status
[Public business definition]
Driver finishing-status lookup referenced by results.statusId. status is the human-readable result status. It is distinct from championship rank and constructorResults.status. Registered stored-row key: statusId.

BIRD formula_1 table seasons
[Public business definition]
Championship season records identified by year. A season contains multiple race rounds; season records do not contain individual race results or cumulative driver scores. Registered stored-row key: year.

question: For all the drivers who finished the game in race No. 592, who is the oldest?
sql: SELECT t1.forename, t1.surname FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.status AS t3 ON t2."statusId" = t3."statusId" WHERE t2."raceId" = 592 AND t3.status = 'Finished' ORDER BY t1.dob ASC LIMIT 1

gold_sql: SELECT T1.forename, T1.surname FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN results AS T2 ON T2.driverId = T1.driverId WHERE T2.raceId = 592 AND NOT T2.time IS NULL AND NOT T1.dob IS NULL ORDER BY T1.dob ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. [Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table pitStops; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Pit-stop events for a driver during a race; stop numbers identify successive stops for that driver in that race, while lap identifies when a stop occurred. A driver can make several stops. duration and milliseconds describe the elapsed stop duration.

question: For the driver who set the fastest lap speed, what is his nationality?
sql: SELECT T2.nationality FROM bird_formula_1.results AS T1 JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" ORDER BY CAST(T1."fastestLapSpeed" AS DOUBLE PRECISION) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT
  T2.nationality
FROM
  bird_formula_1.results AS T1
  JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId"
ORDER BY
  CAST(T1."fastestLapSpeed" AS DOUBLE PRECISION) DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT
  1
```

question: State the driver with the most points scored. Find his full name with that points.
sql: SELECT t1.forename, t1.surname, SUM(t2.points) FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" GROUP BY t1."driverId", t1.forename, t1.surname ORDER BY SUM(t2.points) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a driver at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position at that snapshot. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorResults; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor results for individual races, relating a race and constructor. points are awarded for the race result, whereas constructorStandings points are cumulative championship snapshots. status belongs to the constructor race result, not the driver status lookup. Registered stored-row key: constructorResultsId.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorStandings; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a constructor at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table lapTimes; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Lap timing observations for drivers in races. The observation grain is a driver and lap within a race (raceId, driverId, lap); one driver has many lap observations. milliseconds measures the duration of that lap. The drivers table supplies the identity and name of the driver. An observation is not a unique driver.

question: Calculate the percentage whereby Hamilton was not at the 1st track of the the f1 circuit since 2010.
sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1.position <> 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t1."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t2.surname = 'Hamilton' AND t3.year >= 2010
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1.position != 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*)
FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1
JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId"
JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t1."raceId" = t3."raceId"
WHERE t2.surname = 'Hamilton' AND t3.year >= 2010
```
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.position <> 1 THEN T2.position END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T2.driverStandingsId), 0) FROM races AS T1 INNER JOIN driverStandings AS T2 ON T2.raceId = T1.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T3.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T3.surname = 'Hamilton' AND T1.year >= 2010
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T2."position" <> 1 THEN T2."position" END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T2."driverStandingsId"), 0) FROM "races" AS T1 INNER JOIN "driverStandings" AS T2 ON T2."raceId" = T1."raceId" INNER JOIN "drivers" AS T3 ON T3."driverId" = T2."driverId" WHERE T3."surname" = 'Hamilton' AND T1."year" >= 2010

question: Which was Lewis Hamilton first race? What was his points recorded for his first race event?
sql: SELECT T2.name, T1.points FROM bird_formula_1.results AS T1 INNER JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS T2 ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId" INNER JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS T3 ON T1."driverId" = T3."driverId" WHERE T3.forename = 'Lewis' AND T3.surname = 'Hamilton' ORDER BY T2.date ASC, T2.round ASC LIMIT 1
gold_sql: SELECT T1.name, T2.points FROM races AS T1 INNER JOIN driverStandings AS T2 ON T2.raceId = T1.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T3.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T3.forename = 'Lewis' AND T3.surname = 'Hamilton' ORDER BY T1.year ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: Among all European Grand Prix races, what is the percentage of the races were hosted in Germany?
sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t2.country = 'Germany' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_formula_1.races AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.circuits AS t2 ON t1."circuitId" = t2."circuitId" WHERE t1.name = 'European Grand Prix'
raw_sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t2.country = 'Germany' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_formula_1.races AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.circuits AS t2 ON t1."circuitId" = t2."circuitId" WHERE t1.name = 'European Grand Prix'
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1.country = 'Germany' THEN T2.circuitID END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T2.circuitId), 0) FROM circuits AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 ON T2.circuitID = T1.circuitId WHERE T2.name = 'European Grand Prix'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T1."country" = 'Germany' THEN T2."circuitId" END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T2."circuitId"), 0) FROM "circuits" AS T1 INNER JOIN "races" AS T2 ON T2."circuitId" = T1."circuitId" WHERE T2."name" = 'European Grand Prix'

question: Which driver ranked the first in the Canadian Grand Prix in 2007? Please give his reference name.
sql: SELECT t1."driverRef" FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t2."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t3.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND t3.year = 2007 AND t2.position = 1
raw_sql: SELECT t1."driverRef" FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t2."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t3.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND t3.year = 2007 AND t2.position = 1
gold_sql: SELECT T3.forename, T3.surname, T3.driverRef FROM races AS T1 INNER JOIN results AS T2 ON T2.raceId = T1.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T3.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T1.name = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND T2.rank = 1 AND T1.year = 2007
gold_execution_sql: SELECT T3."forename", T3."surname", T3."driverRef" FROM "races" AS T1 INNER JOIN "results" AS T2 ON T2."raceId" = T1."raceId" INNER JOIN "drivers" AS T3 ON T3."driverId" = T2."driverId" WHERE T1."name" = 'Canadian Grand Prix' AND T2."rank" = 1 AND T1."year" = 2007

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table status
[Public business definition]
Driver finishing-status lookup referenced by results.statusId. status is the human-readable result status. It is distinct from championship rank and constructorResults.status. Registered stored-row key: statusId.

BIRD formula_1 table circuits
[Public business definition]
Race circuit entities with name, location/country and geographic coordinates. A circuit can host many races across years; circuit identity differs from race name and race identity. Registered stored-row key: circuitId.

BIRD formula_1 table races; foreign keys: circuitId -> circuits.circuitId, year -> seasons.year
[Public business definition]
Individual scheduled race events with championship year, round, circuit, name, date and start time. raceId identifies an event; the same race name can occur in multiple years. Round orders races within a season. Registered stored-row key: raceId.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorResults; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor results for individual races, relating a race and constructor. points are awarded for the race result, whereas constructorStandings points are cumulative championship snapshots. status belongs to the constructor race result, not the driver status lookup. Registered stored-row key: constructorResultsId.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorStandings; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a constructor at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

Driver qualifying results at a race, including qualifying position and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 segment times. Later segment times can be absent when the driver did not advance. These are qualifying times and positions, not the race finishing result.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table lapTimes; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Lap timing observations for drivers in races. The observation grain is a driver and lap within a race (raceId, driverId, lap); one driver has many lap observations. milliseconds measures the duration of that lap. The drivers table supplies the identity and name of the driver. An observation is not a unique driver.

BIRD formula_1 table races; foreign keys: circuitId -> circuits.circuitId, year -> seasons.year
[Public business definition]
Individual scheduled race events with championship year, round, circuit, name, date and start time. raceId identifies an event; the same race name can occur in multiple years. Round orders races within a season. Registered stored-row key: raceId.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a driver at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position at that snapshot. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

question: Among the drivers that finished the race in the 2008 Chinese Grand Prix, how many of them have participated in Formula_1 races?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1."driverId") FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t2 ON t1."raceId" = t2."raceId" WHERE t2.year = 2008 AND t2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND t1."statusId" = 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1."driverId")
FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1
JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t2 ON t1."raceId" = t2."raceId"
WHERE t2.year = 2008
  AND t2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix'
  AND t1."statusId" = 1;
```
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT T1.driverId FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId WHERE T2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND T2.year = 2008 AND T1.time IS NOT NULL GROUP BY T1.driverId HAVING COUNT(T2.raceId) > 0) AS subquery
gold_execution_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT T1."driverId" FROM "results" AS T1 INNER JOIN "races" AS T2 ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId" WHERE T2."name" = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND T2."year" = 2008 AND T1."time" IS NOT NULL GROUP BY T1."driverId" HAVING COUNT(T2."raceId") > 0) AS subquery

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table constructors
[Public business definition]
Constructor identity records with name, reference and nationality. Constructors relate to race results and championship standings; constructor nationality differs from driver nationality and circuit country. Registered stored-row key: constructorId.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorResults; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor results for individual races, relating a race and constructor. points are awarded for the race result, whereas constructorStandings points are cumulative championship snapshots. status belongs to the constructor race result, not the driver status lookup. Registered stored-row key: constructorResultsId.

BIRD formula_1 table constructorStandings; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Constructor championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a constructor at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a driver at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position at that snapshot. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table qualifying; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver qualifying results at a race, including qualifying position and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 segment times. Later segment times can be absent when the driver did not advance. These are qualifying times and positions, not the race finishing result.

question: Please calculate the race completion percentage of Japanese drivers from 2007 to 2009.
sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1."statusId" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t1."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t2.nationality = 'Japanese' AND t3.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009
raw_sql: SELECT 100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN t1."statusId" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) FROM bird_formula_1.results AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t1."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t2.nationality = 'Japanese' AND t3.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT T1.time IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1.raceId), 0) FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T1.driverId = T3.driverId WHERE T3.nationality = 'Japanese' AND T2.year BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT T1."time" IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1."raceId"), 0) FROM "results" AS T1 INNER JOIN "races" AS T2 ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId" INNER JOIN "drivers" AS T3 ON T1."driverId" = T3."driverId" WHERE T3."nationality" = 'Japanese' AND T2."year" BETWEEN 2007 AND 2009

question: From 2000 to 2005, what percentage of drivers who were born before 1985 and the lap numbers were over 50?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(t1.dob FROM 1 FOR 4) < '1985' AND t2.laps > 50 THEN t1."driverId" END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t1."driverId"), 0) FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t2."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t3.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005
raw_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN SUBSTR(t1.dob, 1, 4) < '1985' AND t2.laps > 50 THEN t1."driverId" END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t1."driverId"), 0) FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.results AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS t3 ON t2."raceId" = t3."raceId" WHERE t3.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005;
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST(T3.dob AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') < '1985' AND T1.laps > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) FROM results AS T1 INNER JOIN races AS T2 ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId INNER JOIN drivers AS T3 ON T1.driverId = T3.driverId WHERE T2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST(T3."dob" AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') < '1985' AND T1."laps" > 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) FROM "results" AS T1 INNER JOIN "races" AS T2 ON T1."raceId" = T2."raceId" INNER JOIN "drivers" AS T3 ON T1."driverId" = T3."driverId" WHERE T2."year" BETWEEN 2000 AND 2005

question: How many French drivers who obtain the laptime less than 02:00.00?
sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1."driverId") FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_formula_1."lapTimes" AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" WHERE t1.nationality = 'French' AND t2.milliseconds < 120000
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(T1.driverId) FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN lapTimes AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId WHERE T1.nationality = 'French' AND (EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM T2.time::INTERVAL) * 60 + EXTRACT(SECOND FROM T2.time::INTERVAL)) < 120
gold_execution_sql: SELECT COUNT(T1."driverId") FROM "drivers" AS T1 INNER JOIN "lapTimes" AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" WHERE T1."nationality" = 'French' AND (EXTRACT(MINUTE FROM CAST(T2."time" AS INTERVAL)) * 60 + EXTRACT(SECOND FROM CAST(T2."time" AS INTERVAL))) < 120

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table constructors
[Public business definition]
Constructor identity records with name, reference and nationality. Constructors relate to race results and championship standings; constructor nationality differs from driver nationality and circuit country. Registered stored-row key: constructorId.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table lapTimes; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Lap timing observations for drivers in races. The observation grain is a driver and lap within a race (raceId, driverId, lap); one driver has many lap observations. milliseconds measures the duration of that lap. The drivers table supplies the identity and name of the driver. An observation is not a unique driver.

BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a driver at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position at that snapshot. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table pitStops; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Pit-stop events for a driver during a race; stop numbers identify successive stops for that driver in that race, while lap identifies when a stop occurred. A driver can make several stops. duration and milliseconds describe the elapsed stop duration.

sql: WITH top_3_youngest AS (SELECT code, nationality FROM bird_formula_1.drivers WHERE dob IS NOT NULL ORDER BY dob DESC LIMIT 3) SELECT code, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM top_3_youngest WHERE nationality = 'Dutch') FROM top_3_youngest

```sql
WITH top_3_youngest AS (
    SELECT code, nationality
    FROM bird_formula_1.drivers
    WHERE dob IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY dob DESC
    LIMIT 3
)
SELECT
    code,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM top_3_youngest WHERE nationality = 'Dutch')
FROM top_3_youngest;
```

question: List down top 3 German drivers who has the shortest average pit stop duration and were born between 1980-1985.
sql: SELECT t1.forename, t1.surname FROM bird_formula_1.drivers AS t1 JOIN bird_formula_1.pitStops AS t2 ON t1."driverId" = t2."driverId" WHERE t1.nationality = 'German' AND SUBSTRING(t1.dob FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1985' GROUP BY t1."driverId", t1.forename, t1.surname ORDER BY AVG(t2.milliseconds) ASC LIMIT 3

BIRD formula_1 table pitStops; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Pit-stop events for a driver during a race; stop numbers identify successive stops for that driver in that race, while lap identifies when a stop occurred. A driver can make several stops. duration and milliseconds describe the elapsed stop duration.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table lapTimes; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Lap timing observations for drivers in races. The observation grain is a driver and lap within a race (raceId, driverId, lap); one driver has many lap observations. milliseconds measures the duration of that lap. The drivers table supplies the identity and name of the driver. An observation is not a unique driver.

BIRD formula_1 table driverStandings; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver championship standings snapshots after a race/round. The business grain is a driver at a season round identified through raceId. points and wins are cumulative within that season, and position is championship position at that snapshot. Successive snapshots overlap; they are not separate race points.

BIRD formula_1 table results; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId, statusId -> status.statusId
[Public business definition]
Driver results for individual races. A result relates a driver to a race. position is the race finishing position, rank is the rank of the driver's fastest lap against other drivers in the race, and points are earned for this single race. This is separate from cumulative championship standings.

BIRD formula_1 table qualifying; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver qualifying results at a race, including qualifying position and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 segment times. Later segment times can be absent when the driver did not advance. These are qualifying times and positions, not the race finishing result.

question: As of the present, what is the full name of the youngest racer? Indicate her nationality and the name of the race to which he/she first joined.
sql: WITH youngest_driver AS (SELECT drivers."driverId", forename || ' ' || surname AS full_name, nationality FROM bird_formula_1.drivers ORDER BY dob DESC LIMIT 1), first_race AS (SELECT r.name AS race_name FROM bird_formula_1.results AS res JOIN bird_formula_1.races AS r ON res."raceId" = r."raceId" WHERE res."driverId" = (SELECT "driverId" FROM youngest_driver) ORDER BY r.date ASC LIMIT 1) SELECT yd.full_name, yd.nationality, fr.race_name FROM youngest_driver AS yd CROSS JOIN first_race AS fr
raw_sql:
```sql
WITH youngest_driver AS (
    SELECT
        "driverId",
        forename || ' ' || surname AS full_name,
        nationality
    FROM bird_formula_1.drivers
    ORDER BY dob DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
first_race AS (
    SELECT
        r.name AS race_name
    FROM bird_formula_1.results res
    JOIN bird_formula_1.races r ON res."raceId" = r."raceId"
    WHERE res."driverId" = (SELECT "driverId" FROM youngest_driver)
    ORDER BY r.date ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
    yd.full_name,
    yd.nationality,
    fr.race_name
FROM youngest_driver yd
CROSS JOIN first_race fr;
```
gold_sql: SELECT T1.forename, T1.surname, T1.nationality, T3.name FROM drivers AS T1 INNER JOIN driverStandings AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId INNER JOIN races AS T3 ON T2.raceId = T3.raceId WHERE T1.dob notnull ORDER BY T1.dob DESC LIMIT 1
gold_execution_sql: SELECT T1."forename", T1."surname", T1."nationality", T3."name" FROM "drivers" AS T1 INNER JOIN "driverStandings" AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" INNER JOIN "races" AS T3 ON T2."raceId" = T3."raceId" WHERE T1."dob" IS NOT NULL ORDER BY T1."dob" DESC LIMIT 1

question: Which top 20 driver created the shortest lap time ever record in a Formula_1 race? Please give them full names.
sql: WITH lap_times_in_seconds AS (SELECT T1."driverId", (CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) * 60 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 2), '.', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 2), '.', 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 2), '.', 2) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(T1."time", ':', 2), '.', 2) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / 1000 ELSE 0 END) AS time_in_seconds FROM bird_formula_1."lapTimes" AS T1) SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname, T1."driverId" FROM (SELECT "driverId", MIN(time_in_seconds) AS min_time_in_seconds FROM lap_times_in_seconds GROUP BY "driverId") AS T1 INNER JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" ORDER BY T1.min_time_in_seconds ASC LIMIT 1
raw_sql: SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname FROM bird_formula_1."lapTimes" AS T1 JOIN bird_formula_1.drivers AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" ORDER BY T1.milliseconds ASC LIMIT 1;
gold_sql: WITH lap_times_in_seconds AS (SELECT driverId, (CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 1) AS float) * 60 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 2), '.', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 2), '.', 1) AS float) ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 2), '.', 2) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART(time, ':', 2), '.', 2) AS float) / 1000 ELSE 0 END) AS time_in_seconds FROM lapTimes) SELECT T2.forename, T2.surname, T1.driverId FROM (SELECT driverId, MIN(time_in_seconds) AS min_time_in_seconds FROM lap_times_in_seconds GROUP BY driverId) AS T1 INNER JOIN drivers AS T2 ON T1.driverId = T2.driverId ORDER BY T1.min_time_in_seconds ASC LIMIT 20
gold_execution_sql: WITH lap_times_in_seconds AS (SELECT "driverId", (CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) * 60 ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 2), '.', 1) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 2), '.', 1) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) ELSE 0 END + CASE WHEN SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 2), '.', 2) <> '' THEN CAST(SPLIT_PART(SPLIT_PART("time", ':', 2), '.', 2) AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / 1000 ELSE 0 END) AS time_in_seconds FROM "lapTimes") SELECT T2."forename", T2."surname", T1."driverId" FROM (SELECT "driverId", MIN(time_in_seconds) AS min_time_in_seconds FROM lap_times_in_seconds GROUP BY "driverId") AS T1 INNER JOIN "drivers" AS T2 ON T1."driverId" = T2."driverId" ORDER BY T1.min_time_in_seconds ASC LIMIT 20

table_hits.description:
BIRD formula_1 table lapTimes; foreign keys: driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Lap timing observations for drivers in races. The observation grain is a driver and lap within a race (raceId, driverId, lap); one driver has many lap observations. milliseconds measures the duration of that lap. The drivers table supplies the identity and name of the driver. An observation is not a unique driver.

BIRD formula_1 table drivers
[Public business definition]
Driver identity records. driverId identifies the driver used by race results, standings, lap timings, pit stops and qualifying. forename and surname are components of the personal name; a driver can participate in many races and have many observation records.

BIRD formula_1 table constructors
[Public business definition]
Constructor identity records with name, reference and nationality. Constructors relate to race results and championship standings; constructor nationality differs from driver nationality and circuit country. Registered stored-row key: constructorId.

BIRD formula_1 table qualifying; foreign keys: constructorId -> constructors.constructorId, driverId -> drivers.driverId, raceId -> races.raceId
[Public business definition]
Driver qualifying results at a race, including qualifying position and the Q1, Q2 and Q3 segment times. Later segment times can be absent when the driver did not advance. These are qualifying times and positions, not the race finishing result.

BIRD formula_1 table races; foreign keys: circuitId -> circuits.circuitId, year -> seasons.year
[Public business definition]
Individual scheduled race events with championship year, round, circuit, name, date and start time. raceId identifies an event; the same race name can occur in multiple years. Round orders races within a season. Registered stored-row key: raceId.

BIRD formula_1 table seasons
[Public business definition]
Championship season records identified by year. A season contains multiple race rounds; season records do not contain individual race results or cumulative driver scores. Registered stored-row key: year.

question: Which publisher published the slowest superhero?
sql: SELECT t3.publisher_name FROM bird_superhero.hero_attribute AS t1 JOIN bird_superhero.attribute AS t2 ON t1.attribute_id = t2.id JOIN bird_superhero.superhero AS t4 ON t1.hero_id = t4.id JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t3 ON t4.publisher_id = t3.id WHERE t2.attribute_name = 'Speed' ORDER BY t1.attribute_value ASC LIMIT 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT t3.publisher_name
FROM bird_superhero.hero_attribute AS t1
JOIN bird_superhero.attribute AS t2 ON t1.attribute_id = t2.id
JOIN bird_superhero.superhero AS t4 ON t1.hero_id = t4.id
JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t3 ON t4.publisher_id = t3.id
WHERE t2.attribute_name = 'Speed'
ORDER BY t1.attribute_value ASC
LIMIT 1;
```
gold_sql: SELECT T2.publisher_name FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN publisher AS T2 ON T1.publisher_id = T2.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS T3 ON T1.id = T3.hero_id INNER JOIN attribute AS T4 ON T3.attribute_id = T4.id WHERE T4.attribute_name = 'Speed' ORDER BY T3.attribute_value NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: What is the percentage of superheroes who act in their own self-interest or make decisions based on their own moral code? Indicate how many of the said superheroes were published by Marvel Comics.
sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN t2.alignment = 'Neutral' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(t1.id), COUNT(CASE WHEN t2.alignment = 'Neutral' AND t3.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN t1.id ELSE NULL END) FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS t1 LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t3 ON t1.publisher_id = t3.id
raw_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN t2.alignment = 'Neutral' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / COUNT(t1.id), COUNT(CASE WHEN t2.alignment = 'Neutral' AND t3.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' THEN t1.id ELSE NULL END) FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS t1 LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t3 ON t1.publisher_id = t3.id

question: Which superhero has the most durability published by Dark Horse Comics?
sql: SELECT t1.superhero_name FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS t1 JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t2 ON t1.publisher_id = t2.id JOIN bird_superhero.hero_attribute AS t3 ON t1.id = t3.hero_id JOIN bird_superhero.attribute AS t4 ON t3.attribute_id = t4.id WHERE t2.publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics' AND t4.attribute_name = 'Durability' ORDER BY t3.attribute_value DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT
  t1.superhero_name
FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS t1
JOIN bird_superhero.publisher AS t2
  ON t1.publisher_id = t2.id
JOIN bird_superhero.hero_attribute AS t3
  ON t1.id = t3.hero_id
JOIN bird_superhero.attribute AS t4
  ON t3.attribute_id = t4.id
WHERE
  t2.publisher_name = 'Dark Horse Comics'
  AND t4.attribute_name = 'Durability'
ORDER BY
  t3.attribute_value DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

question: What is the percentage of blue female superheroes among all female superheroes?
sql: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS T1 JOIN bird_superhero.gender AS T3 ON T1.gender_id = T3.id LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.colour AS T2 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T2.id WHERE T3.gender = 'Female'
raw_sql: SELECT COUNT(CASE WHEN T2.colour = 'Blue' THEN 1 END) * 100.0 / COUNT(*) FROM bird_superhero.superhero AS T1 JOIN bird_superhero.gender AS T3 ON T1.gender_id = T3.id LEFT JOIN bird_superhero.colour AS T2 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T2.id WHERE T3.gender = 'Female'
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T3.colour = 'Blue' THEN T1.id ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1.id), 0) FROM superhero AS T1 INNER JOIN gender AS T2 ON T1.gender_id = T2.id INNER JOIN colour AS T3 ON T1.skin_colour_id = T3.id WHERE T2.gender = 'Female'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(COUNT(CASE WHEN T3."colour" = 'Blue' THEN T1."id" ELSE NULL END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1."id"), 0) FROM "superhero" AS T1 INNER JOIN "gender" AS T2 ON T1."gender_id" = T2."id" INNER JOIN "colour" AS T3 ON T1."skin_colour_id" = T3."id" WHERE T2."gender" = 'Female'

table_hits.description:
BIRD codebase_community table users
[Public business definition]
User profile entities with display name, reputation and profile activity/registration dates. Reputation differs from post Score; Views counts profile views. A display name is not a guaranteed unique user identifier. Registered stored-row key: Id.

BIRD codebase_community table comments; foreign keys: PostId -> posts.Id, UserId -> users.Id
[Public business definition]
Comment records on posts, linked by PostId and authored by UserId when present. Comment Score is separate from post Score and user Reputation. Multiple comments may belong to one post or author. Registered stored-row key: Id.

BIRD codebase_community table posts; foreign keys: LastEditorUserId -> users.Id, OwnerUserId -> users.Id, ParentId -> posts.Id
[Public business definition]
Question/answer post entities. PostTypeId distinguishes post types; ParentId relates an answer to its parent question, and AcceptedAnswerId references an accepted answer. OwnerUserId is the author. Stored AnswerCount, CommentCount, ViewCount and Score represent different measures. Registered stored-row key: Id.

BIRD codebase_community table votes; foreign keys: PostId -> posts.Id, UserId -> users.Id
[Public business definition]
Vote events linked to posts, with VoteTypeId describing the event type and optional user/bounty information. Multiple votes may reference one post; vote counts differ from stored net post score. Registered stored-row key: Id.

BIRD codebase_community table postHistory; foreign keys: PostId -> posts.Id, UserId -> users.Id
[Public business definition]
Post revision/history events with type, revision identifier, event date and editor. History text and event comments differ from current posts.Body and comments.Text. A post can have many events. Registered stored-row key: Id.

BIRD codebase_community table tags; foreign keys: ExcerptPostId -> posts.Id
[Public business definition]
Tag entities with TagName, stored usage Count and links to excerpt/wiki posts. A tag usage count is not a user count or a count of tag dictionary records. Registered stored-row key: Id.

gold_sql: SELECT AVG(T2.ViewCount) AS AverageViewCount, T2.Title, T1.Text FROM comments AS T1 INNER JOIN posts AS T2 ON T2.Id = T1.PostId WHERE T2.Tags = '<humor>' GROUP BY T2.Title, T1.Text

question: Which user have only one post history per post and having at least 1000 views?
sql: SELECT t1."Id" FROM bird_codebase_community.users AS t1 JOIN bird_codebase_community.postHistory AS t2 ON t1."Id" = t2."UserId" WHERE t1."Views" >= 1000 GROUP BY t1."Id" HAVING COUNT(t2."Id") = COUNT(DISTINCT t2."PostId")
raw_sql: SELECT t1."Id" FROM bird_codebase_community.users AS t1 JOIN bird_codebase_community.postHistory AS t2 ON t1."Id" = t2."UserId" WHERE t1."Views" >= 1000 GROUP BY t1."Id" HAVING COUNT(t2."Id") = COUNT(DISTINCT t2."PostId")
gold_sql: SELECT T2.UserId FROM users AS T1 INNER JOIN postHistory AS T2 ON T1.Id = T2.UserId INNER JOIN posts AS T3 ON T2.PostId = T3.Id WHERE T3.ViewCount >= 1000 GROUP BY T2.UserId HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T2.PostHistoryTypeId) = 1
gold_execution_sql: SELECT T2."UserId" FROM "users" AS T1 INNER JOIN "postHistory" AS T2 ON T1."Id" = T2."UserId" INNER JOIN "posts" AS T3 ON T2."PostId" = T3."Id" WHERE T3."ViewCount" >= 1000 GROUP BY T2."UserId" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT T2."PostHistoryTypeId") = 1

question: What is the percentage difference of student badges given during 2010 and 2011?

gold_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST(Date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2010' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(Id), 0) - CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST(Date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY') = '2011' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(Id), 0) FROM badges WHERE Name = 'Student'

```sql
SELECT

  t1."UpVotes"
FROM bird_codebase_community.users AS t1
```

BIRD codebase_community table badges; foreign keys: UserId -> users.Id
[Public business definition]

table_hits.description:
BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. The name of a card can occur on more than one printing. type is the complete visible type line, including supertypes and subtypes; types stores the card-type categories. Each printing can have foreign-language data, format legalities and official rulings in the related detail tables.

BIRD card_games table foreign_data; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Foreign-language properties of a card printing, from the printing's foreignData list. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; language identifies the language and name is the localized card name. A card can have multiple language records. Presence of one language row does not establish the absence of another language for that card.

BIRD card_games table sets
[Public business definition]
Magic card set metadata. code identifies the set referenced by card setCode. Release date, set type and set-level flags describe the set, while card face and printing attributes belong to cards. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table rulings; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Official rulings attached to a card printing, from its rulings list. uuid associates each ruling with the card printing. date and text describe a ruling; a printing can have multiple ruling records.

BIRD card_games table legalities; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Play-format legalities of a card printing, from the printing's legalities mapping. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; format identifies the play format and status describes legality in that format. A printing can have multiple format records with different statuses.

BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

table_hits.description:
BIRD card_games table legalities; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Play-format legalities of a card printing, from the printing's legalities mapping. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; format identifies the play format and status describes legality in that format. A printing can have multiple format records with different statuses.

BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. The name of a card can occur on more than one printing. type is the complete visible type line, including supertypes and subtypes; types stores the card-type categories. Each printing can have foreign-language data, format legalities and official rulings in the related detail tables.

BIRD card_games table sets
[Public business definition]
Magic card set metadata. code identifies the set referenced by card setCode. Release date, set type and set-level flags describe the set, while card face and printing attributes belong to cards. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table rulings; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Official rulings attached to a card printing, from its rulings list. uuid associates each ruling with the card printing. date and text describe a ruling; a printing can have multiple ruling records.

BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table foreign_data; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Foreign-language properties of a card printing, from the printing's foreignData list. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; language identifies the language and name is the localized card name. A card can have multiple language records. Presence of one language row does not establish the absence of another language for that card.

table_hits.description:
BIRD card_games table rulings; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Official rulings attached to a card printing, from its rulings list. uuid associates each ruling with the card printing. date and text describe a ruling; a printing can have multiple ruling records.

BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. The name of a card can occur on more than one printing. type is the complete visible type line, including supertypes and subtypes; types stores the card-type categories. Each printing can have foreign-language data, format legalities and official rulings in the related detail tables.

BIRD card_games table foreign_data; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Foreign-language properties of a card printing, from the printing's foreignData list. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; language identifies the language and name is the localized card name. A card can have multiple language records. Presence of one language row does not establish the absence of another language for that card.

BIRD card_games table sets
[Public business definition]
Magic card set metadata. code identifies the set referenced by card setCode. Release date, set type and set-level flags describe the set, while card face and printing attributes belong to cards. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table legalities; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Play-format legalities of a card printing, from the printing's legalities mapping. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; format identifies the play format and status describes legality in that format. A printing can have multiple format records with different statuses.

BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

question: Name the card and artist with the most ruling information. Also state if the card is a promotional printing.
sql: SELECT cards.name, cards.artist, cards."isPromo" FROM bird_card_games.cards JOIN bird_card_games.rulings ON cards.uuid = rulings.uuid GROUP BY cards.id, cards.name, cards.artist, cards."isPromo" ORDER BY COUNT(rulings.id) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
gold_sql: SELECT T1.name, T1.artist, T1.isPromo FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN rulings AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.isPromo = 1 AND T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) = (SELECT MAX(count_uuid) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uuid) AS count_uuid FROM cards WHERE isPromo = 1 GROUP BY artist) AS subquery)) LIMIT 1
gold_execution_sql: SELECT T1."name", T1."artist", T1."isPromo" FROM "cards" AS T1 INNER JOIN "rulings" AS T2 ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid" WHERE T1."isPromo" = 1 AND T1."artist" = (SELECT "artist" FROM "cards" WHERE "isPromo" = 1 GROUP BY "artist" HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT "uuid") = (SELECT MAX(count_uuid) FROM (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT "uuid") AS count_uuid FROM "cards" WHERE "isPromo" = 1 GROUP BY "artist") AS subquery)) LIMIT 1

sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t2.language = 'Chinese Simplified' THEN t1.id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id), 0) FROM bird_card_games.cards AS t1 LEFT JOIN bird_card_games.foreign_data AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid
raw_sql:

```sql
SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t2.language = 'Chinese Simplified' THEN t1.id END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id), 0)
FROM bird_card_games.cards AS t1
LEFT JOIN bird_card_games.foreign_data AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid
```

BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code

Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

sql: SELECT bird_card_games.foreign_data.name FROM bird_card_games.cards JOIN bird_card_games.foreign_data ON bird_card_games.cards.uuid = bird_card_games.foreign_data.uuid WHERE bird_card_games.foreign_data.language = 'French' AND bird_card_games.cards.type LIKE '%Creature%' AND bird_card_games.cards.layout = 'normal' AND bird_card_games.cards."borderColor" = 'black' AND bird_card_games.cards.artist = 'Matthew D. Wilson'
raw_sql: SELECT bird_card_games.foreign_data.name FROM bird_card_games.cards JOIN bird_card_games.foreign_data ON bird_card_games.cards.uuid = bird_card_games.foreign_data.uuid WHERE bird_card_games.foreign_data.language = 'French' AND bird_card_games.cards.type LIKE '%Creature%' AND bird_card_games.cards.layout = 'normal' AND bird_card_games.cards."borderColor" = 'black' AND bird_card_games.cards.artist = 'Matthew D. table_hits.description:
BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. The name of a card can occur on more than one printing. type is the complete visible type line, including supertypes and subtypes; types stores the card-type categories. Each printing can have foreign-language data, format legalities and official rulings in the related detail tables.

BIRD card_games table foreign_data; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Foreign-language properties of a card printing, from the printing's foreignData list. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; language identifies the language and name is the localized card name. A card can have multiple language records. Presence of one language row does not establish the absence of another language for that card.

BIRD card_games table sets
[Public business definition]
Magic card set metadata. code identifies the set referenced by card setCode. Release date, set type and set-level flags describe the set, while card face and printing attributes belong to cards. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table rulings; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Official rulings attached to a card printing, from its rulings list. uuid associates each ruling with the card printing. date and text describe a ruling; a printing can have multiple ruling records.

BIRD card_games table legalities; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Play-format legalities of a card printing, from the printing's legalities mapping. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; format identifies the play format and status describes legality in that format. A printing can have multiple format records with different statuses.

question: What percentage of cards without power are in French?
sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bird_card_games.foreign_data WHERE foreign_data.uuid = cards.uuid AND foreign_data.language = 'French') THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_card_games.cards WHERE power IS NULL

gold_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN T2.language = 'French' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1.id), 0) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.power IS NULL OR T1.power = '*'

BIRD card_games table cards; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Card printings associated with sets. uuid is MTGJSON's unique identifier and setCode is the printing set code. The name of a card can occur on more than one printing. type is the complete visible type line, including supertypes and subtypes; types stores the card-type categories. Each printing can have foreign-language data, format legalities and official rulings in the related detail tables.

BIRD card_games table rulings; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Official rulings attached to a card printing, from its rulings list. uuid associates each ruling with the card printing. date and text describe a ruling; a printing can have multiple ruling records.

BIRD card_games table foreign_data; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Foreign-language properties of a card printing, from the printing's foreignData list. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; language identifies the language and name is the localized card name. A card can have multiple language records. Presence of one language row does not establish the absence of another language for that card.

BIRD card_games table set_translations; foreign keys: setCode -> sets.code
[Public business definition]
Language-specific translations of set names. setCode links to the set and language identifies the translation language. Multiple translations can exist for one set; translation rows are not distinct sets. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table sets
[Public business definition]
Magic card set metadata. code identifies the set referenced by card setCode. Release date, set type and set-level flags describe the set, while card face and printing attributes belong to cards. Registered stored-row key: id.

BIRD card_games table legalities; foreign keys: uuid -> cards.uuid
[Public business definition]
Play-format legalities of a card printing, from the printing's legalities mapping. uuid associates the detail with the card printing; format identifies the play format and status describes legality in that format. A printing can have multiple format records with different statuses.

question: What's the Italian name of the set of cards with "Ancestor's Chosen" is in?
sql: SELECT bird_card_games.set_translations.translation FROM bird_card_games.set_translations INNER JOIN bird_card_games.cards ON bird_card_games.set_translations."setCode" = bird_card_games.cards."setCode" WHERE bird_card_games.cards.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen' AND bird_card_games.set_translations.language = 'Italian'
raw_sql:

```sql
SELECT bird_card_games.set_translations.translation FROM bird_card_games.set_translations INNER JOIN bird_card_games.cards ON bird_card_games.set_translations."setCode" = bird_card_games.cards."setCode" WHERE bird_card_games.cards.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen' AND bird_card_games.set_translations.language = 'Italian'
```
gold_sql: SELECT translation FROM set_translations WHERE setCode IN (SELECT setCode FROM cards WHERE name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen') AND language = 'Italian'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT "translation" FROM "set_translations" WHERE "setCode" IN (SELECT "setCode" FROM "cards" WHERE "name" = 'Ancestor''s Chosen') AND "language" = 'Italian'

question: For the set of cards with "Ancestor's Chosen" in it, is there a Korean version of it?
sql: SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bird_card_games.set_translations WHERE set_translations."setCode" IN (SELECT cards."setCode" FROM bird_card_games.cards WHERE name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen') AND language = 'Korean')
raw_sql:
SELECT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM bird_card_games.set_translations

question: What is the percentage of incredibly powerful cards in the set Coldsnap?
sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN CAST(cards.power AS DECIMAL) > 5 THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_card_games.cards JOIN bird_card_games.sets ON cards."setCode" = sets.code WHERE sets.name = 'Coldsnap' AND cards.power ~ '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
raw_sql: SELECT 100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN CAST(cards.power AS NUMERIC) > 5 THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*) FROM bird_card_games.cards JOIN bird_card_games.sets ON cards."setCode" = sets.code WHERE sets.name = 'Coldsnap' AND cards.power ~ '^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
gold_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT T1.cardKingdomFoilId IS NULL AND NOT T1.cardKingdomId IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1.id), 0) FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN sets AS T2 ON T2.code = T1.setCode WHERE T2.name = 'Coldsnap'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN NOT T1."cardKingdomFoilId" IS NULL AND NOT T1."cardKingdomId" IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS REAL) * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(T1."id"), 0) FROM "cards" AS T1 INNER JOIN "sets" AS T2 ON T2."code" = T1."setCode" WHERE T2."name" = 'Coldsnap'

question: Find and list the names of sets which doesn't have Japanese translation but have Korean translation.
sql: SELECT s.name FROM bird_card_games.sets AS s WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bird_card_games.set_translations AS st_ko WHERE st_ko."setCode" = s.code AND st_ko.language = 'Korean') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bird_card_games.set_translations AS st_ja WHERE st_ja."setCode" = s.code AND st_ja.language = 'Japanese')
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT
  s.name
FROM bird_card_games.sets AS s
WHERE EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM bird_card_games.set_translations AS st_ko
  WHERE st_ko."setCode" = s.code
    AND st_ko.language = 'Korean'
)
AND NOT EXISTS (
  SELECT 1
  FROM bird_card_games.set_translations AS st_ja
  WHERE st_ja."setCode" = s.code
    AND st_ja.language = 'Japanese'
)
```
gold_sql: SELECT name FROM sets WHERE code IN (SELECT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Korean' AND NOT language LIKE '%Japanese%')
gold_execution_sql: SELECT "name" FROM "sets" WHERE "code" IN (SELECT "setCode" FROM "set_translations" WHERE "language" = 'Korean' AND NOT "language" LIKE '%Japanese%')

question: List all the frame styles and cards Allen Williams worked on and find any banned cards if there are any.
sql: SELECT DISTINCT cards."frameVersion", cards.name, CASE WHEN legalities.status = 'Banned' THEN cards.name ELSE 'NO' END FROM bird_card_games.cards AS cards INNER JOIN bird_card_games.legalities AS legalities ON cards.uuid = legalities.uuid WHERE cards.artist = 'Allen Williams'
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT DISTINCT
  cards.name,
  cards."frameVersion",
  legalities.status
FROM bird_card_games.cards AS cards
LEFT JOIN bird_card_games.legalities AS legalities
  ON cards.uuid = legalities.uuid
  AND LOWER(legalities.status) = 'banned'
WHERE cards.artist = 'Allen Williams';
```
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.frameVersion, T1.name, CASE WHEN T2.status = 'Banned' THEN T1.name ELSE 'NO' END FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = 'Allen Williams'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1."frameVersion", T1."name", CASE WHEN T2."status" = 'Banned' THEN T1."name" ELSE 'NO' END FROM "cards" AS T1 INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2 ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid" WHERE T1."artist" = 'Allen Williams'

question: Which type of label is the most numerous in atoms with hydrogen?
sql: SELECT t2.label FROM bird_toxicology.atom AS t1 INNER JOIN bird_toxicology.molecule AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id WHERE t1.element = 'h' GROUP BY t2.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT t2.label
FROM bird_toxicology.atom AS t1
INNER JOIN bird_toxicology.molecule AS t2
  ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id
WHERE t1.element = 'h'
GROUP BY t2.label
ORDER BY count(*) DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
gold_sql: SELECT T.label FROM (SELECT T2.label, COUNT(T2.molecule_id) FROM atom AS T1 INNER JOIN molecule AS T2 ON T1.molecule_id = T2.molecule_id WHERE T1.element = 'h' GROUP BY T2.label ORDER BY COUNT(T2.molecule_id) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AS t
gold_execution_sql: SELECT T."label" FROM (SELECT T2."label", COUNT(T2."molecule_id") FROM "atom" AS T1 INNER JOIN "molecule" AS T2 ON T1."molecule_id" = T2."molecule_id" WHERE T1."element" = 'h' GROUP BY T2."label" ORDER BY COUNT(T2."molecule_id") DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AS t

question: How many atoms with iodine and with sulfur type elements are there in single bond molecules?
sql: SELECT COUNT(atom.atom_id) FROM bird_toxicology.atom AS atom WHERE atom.element IN ('i', 's') AND atom.molecule_id IN (SELECT bond.molecule_id FROM bird_toxicology.bond AS bond WHERE bond.bond_type = '-')
raw_sql:
```sql
SELECT COUNT(atom.atom_id) FROM bird_toxicology.atom AS atom WHERE atom.element IN ('i', 's') AND atom.molecule_id IN (SELECT bond.molecule_id FROM bird_toxicology.bond AS bond WHERE bond.bond_type = '-')
```
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.element = 'i' THEN T1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS iodine_nums, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1.element = 's' THEN T1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS sulfur_nums FROM atom AS T1 INNER JOIN connected AS T2 ON T1.atom_id = T2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS T3 ON T2.bond_id = T3.bond_id WHERE T3.bond_type = '-'
gold_execution_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1."element" = 'i' THEN T1."atom_id" ELSE NULL END) AS iodine_nums, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN T1."element" = 's' THEN T1."atom_id" ELSE NULL END) AS sulfur_nums FROM "atom" AS T1 INNER JOIN "connected" AS T2 ON T1."atom_id" = T2."atom_id" INNER JOIN "bond" AS T3 ON T2."bond_id" = T3."bond_id" WHERE T3."bond_type" = '-'
